title: Build a bounded Python-to-Java modernization accelerator with reviewed evidence
requirements: Use Python 3.11+ standard library and an already installed JDK; compile with javac --release 17 and run Java behavior tests locally.
Create only program-owned disposable fixture workspaces; accept no path to a real external repository.
Inventory exact files, sizes and SHA-256 values; enforce eight-file, 32768-byte/file and 131072-byte aggregate limits.
Reject incomplete fixtures, unknown files, symlinks, hard links, nested directories and invalid ownership markers.
Produce a labeled lexical local-class dependency graph, known coverage gaps and reverse-reference blast-radius distances.
Support one exact audited PricePolicy transformation; unsupported source bytes require a new recipe and review.
Dry run must produce a unified patch without modifying source bytes.
Compile both baseline and candidate and execute 43 Java assertions covering values, boundaries, tenant labels and rejection behavior.
Resolve the reviewer from a trusted fixture credential; bind approval to actor, fixture identity, input hash, preview digest and patch hash.
Reject forged identity, changed approval payloads, cross-workspace approval and modified previews.
Detect drift in any inventoried file, including files outside the changed target, before apply.
Revalidate the candidate before the single-file atomic replacement.
Replay the same approved preview without a second write; reject replay after subsequent input drift.
Publish inventory, graph, patch, validation, approval, apply receipt, report and hashed artifact manifest.
Teach Git/CI handoff and other-language adapter contracts as design exercises; execute only Python and Java here.
context: A platform team needs a modernization accelerator, but a generic “replace deprecated code” script has already changed unrelated repositories and claimed success after finding a new string. Your job is to build a small verifiable vertical slice. The fixture has a pricing policy, an invoice consumer, a receipt consumer and an executable behavior probe. The legacy policy creates an Integer only to unbox it immediately for a bounded money calculation. The supported transformation removes that unnecessary local box while retaining validation and long arithmetic. Python must discover the local class-reference structure, identify potential consumers, preview the exact edit, run Java behavior checks and apply only after a bound review decision. This slice deliberately handles no real customer repository and no arbitrary Java syntax. The interview challenge is to explain why these limits make the artifact reviewable, and which additional capabilities would be required before expanding it.
architecture: The Python controller owns a TemporaryDirectory containing the fixture, candidate copies, build outputs and artifacts. It accepts no repository-path parameter. A marker and full manifest bind source identity; link and size checks restrict the fixture shape. A lexical class-reference scanner creates conservative candidate edges, then a reverse walk reports potential dependents with distance. The recipe recognizes the complete target file by an audited hash and chooses a fixed after-version. Baseline and candidate sources are compiled in separate directories using argv subprocess calls, annotation processing disabled and bounded process time. Java executes assertions and emits an observed outcome signature. A preview binds these artifacts to input and patch hashes. A fixture credential resolves a reviewer; a private process-local key signs the approval payload. Apply verifies signature, registry membership and complete snapshot freshness, validates again, then replaces only the target file. A replay ledger returns the existing result when the resulting snapshot still matches. Reports include coverage gaps and artifact hashes. This is a teaching controller, not an OS sandbox or enterprise identity service.

walkthrough.title: 1. Define observable behavior before writing a recipe
walkthrough.body: Start by predicting the fixture outcomes. Unit price 1250 cents and quantity 3 must produce 3750; the maximum permitted pair 1000000×10000 must produce 10000000000 using long arithmetic. Zero unit price is valid; zero quantity is not. The receipt consumer preserves a validated tenant label and rejects null, traversal-like and uppercase labels. These identifiers demonstrate formatting and separation of observed outputs, not authenticated tenant authorization. BehaviorProbe runs 43 checks, including quantities 127 and 128 on opposite sides of a common boxing-cache boundary. The boxed object never escapes the exact supported policy method; removing it therefore does not change an exposed identity contract. A broad replacement of Integer constructors in arbitrary code would need additional identity and nullability analysis. The tests define this fixture's behavior, while the complete target fingerprint defines the supported transformation boundary.

walkthrough.title: 2. Inventory and state graph coverage honestly
walkthrough.body: snapshot reads every permitted fixture file, records byte count and SHA-256 and hashes a canonical sorted manifest. The ownership marker participates in that identity. Byte limits, exact filenames and link rejection prevent accidental expansion into a real repository. lexical_graph strips simple comments and literals, recognizes one matching class per file and records references to other known local classes. This creates candidate dependency edges, not Java method resolution. InvoiceService references PricePolicy; ReceiptApi references InvoiceService; BehaviorProbe references fixture consumers. The reverse traversal finds all three potentially affected classes. Distance ranks proximity only. Reflection, dynamic dispatch, external libraries, build plugins and cross-language calls are listed as gaps. A production implementation should integrate suitable compiler/build/code-context tools and preserve their coverage signals rather than declaring a regex graph complete.

walkthrough.title: 3. Make a narrow supported preview
walkthrough.body: The recipe recognizes the exact before or after PricePolicy bytes by SHA-256. A changed comment, extra branch or altered validation rejects the recipe instead of triggering fuzzy rewriting. For the before-version, the after-file removes the local Integer allocation and directly multiplies unitCents by quantity using the same long conversion and Math.multiplyExact call. unified_diff produces a human-readable patch, but apply does not blindly execute a patch parser: its known preview carries the exact after-content and hash. A fresh candidate copy receives the proposed bytes, leaving the input fixture unchanged. A dry-run checksum test proves that no source write occurred. If the target already has the audited after-version, the preview has no changes and a successful approved apply reports no_change. This is idempotent recipe behavior with a deliberately small support matrix.

walkthrough.title: 4. Compile and run both behavior gates
walkthrough.body: The controller launches javac with--release 17,-encoding UTF-8,-proc:none and a separate class directory, then java with a bounded heap and the BehaviorProbe entry point. Arguments are passed as a list with shell=False; compile/runtime status, stdout and stderr become receipts. Environment options that could inject Java flags or classpaths are removed. A20-second timeout bounds each process. Both Java versions must compile, pass 43 runtime assertions and emit the same outcome signature. The before compiler may warn about the deprecated boxing constructor; that is recorded separately from behavior success. Negative fixtures intentionally return quantity instead of the total and contain invalid Java syntax. The first fails executed assertions; the second fails compilation. Finding a new source string cannot pass either gate. These checks establish the fixture contract, not complete real-application equivalence.

walkthrough.title: 5. Bind review to trusted identity and exact bytes
walkthrough.body: The approval API accepts a fixture credential, not an actor label supplied inside a proposed approval. A private mapping resolves that credential to fixture-reviewer; an unknown credential or the plain actor name is rejected. The controller signs actor, root identity, preview digest, input hash and patch hash with a private ephemeral HMAC key. Apply checks the signature's ASCII hex shape, compares it in constant-time style using compare_digest and verifies every binding. A tampered actor, malformed signature, edited after-content or preview from another fixture is rejected without changing the target. This demonstrates the boundary between identity resolution and a self-asserted field. The public demo credential is intentionally not production authentication. A real service needs an independently authenticated identity, protected signing service, authorization policy, expiration and durable audit. Do not use the demo token to authorize real repository writes.

walkthrough.title: 6. Detect staleness, apply once and replay safely
walkthrough.body: Input identity covers the entire permitted snapshot, so adding a comment to ReceiptApi invalidates an approved PricePolicy preview. Review must then start from a fresh snapshot instead of reusing approval. Before writing, apply reconstructs a candidate and runs the Java gate again; it checks the source snapshot once more afterward. Only one owned source path is replaced atomically. The receipt records changed paths, trusted actor, preview/input/patch identities, resulting snapshot and observed behavior. Repeating the same approval in the same controller process returns already_appliedwhen the resulting snapshot still matches; it does not rewrite the file. Later drift makes replay fail. The key and replay ledger are process-local, so this case claims no restart durability, distributed lock or protection against a hostile process racing filesystem operations. Multi-file or crash-safe application requires a stronger design.

walkthrough.title: 7. Export a reviewable evidence bundle
walkthrough.body: Artifacts contain the inventory, graph, complete preview, unified patch, before/candidate validation, signed approval, apply receipt and report. The artifact manifest stores each payload's path, byte count and SHA-256; its own hash is excluded to avoid a recursive definition. export_report embeds artifact payloads in the JSON printed to stdout, so an optional redirected report remains useful after the temporary workspace is removed. Inspect the source and patch identities,43-check signature, changed path and graph gaps. A passing report should say exactly what was executed and which input it describes. Hashes identify bytes; they do not establish correctness or external authenticity by themselves. This evidence can accompany a proposed change, but the demo neither commits nor pushes anything and never applies to a real repository.

walkthrough.title: 8. Design Git/CI and other-target adapters without pretending they ran
walkthrough.body: For a real Git integration, a Python controller would record the selected base revision and dirty-path policy, create an isolated review workspace, request an approved target-specific adapter and regenerate validation receipts for that exact input. The human would review the patch and artifact bundle before any user-authorized commit or pull-request delivery. CI should run compilation, behavioral and contract tests on the reviewed revision, isolate untrusted code, restrict credentials and preserve artifacts. None of those Git/CI actions occurs here. An adapter for .NET or another language would expose analyze, plan, validate and materialize capabilities, explicit supported versions, coverage gaps and rollback constraints. Python may orchestrate existing compiler or AI-assisted tools, but they must return deterministic patches and actual build/test receipts under the same identity and approval contract. No .NET migration, C# implementation or AI-provider result is claimed by this Python/Java fixture.

assignment.objective: Rebuild the controller in your own Python draft, preserving the narrow recipe, source identity and actual Java parity gates before unlocking the reference.
steps: Download all nine files with their nested paths intact; install nothing automatically. Verify python 3, javac and java are already available. The local validation used Python 3.14.7 andOpenJDK 23.0.2 targeting Java 17.

Four-hour allocation:20 minutes recall,50 minutes mechanisms,30 minutes predicting examples,75 minutes implementing your own controller,40 minutes defending scope/approval/failure behavior and 25 minutes reviewing receipts.
Predict the supported before/after difference and 43-check Java signature, then implement a read-only manifest and lexical graph first. Label graph gaps explicitly.
Implement dry-run candidate copying, exact-target fingerprint recognition and separate javac/java gates. Add a semantic-negative candidate that compiles but fails behavior.
Implement credential-to-actor resolution and approval binding over root/input/preview/patch. Prove self-asserted identity and modified payloads fail.
Add full-snapshot drift checks, one-file apply, in-process replay and artifact export. Keep the callable surface free of arbitrary external repository paths.

Run the provided self-test suite after your own attempts. Compare receipts rather than only source strings. Defend one uncovered real-application behavior and the adapter contract needed to expand safely.

acceptance: Self-test command exits 0 and reports 8 passing unittest methods; all fixtures live in TemporaryDirectory workspaces.
Each successful before/candidate/apply gate compiles and executes BehaviorProbe with exactly 43 checks, receiptA tenant-a:3750 and maximum total 10000000000.
Dry run retains the exact input snapshot hash; only PricePolicy.java appears in the proposed changed paths.
Graph reports InvoiceService→PricePolicy and ReceiptApi→InvoiceService; blast radius contains InvoiceService, ReceiptApi and BehaviorProbe plus explicit gaps.
Unknown reviewer credentials, forged actor/signature, changed preview bytes and cross-fixture reuse raise ApprovalFailure without changing the target.
Any inventoried dependency drift after preview raises StalePreview; same approved apply replays as already_applied and drift after apply rejects replay.
A changed target comment raises UnsupportedRecipe; symlinks, hard links, unknown files, oversized files and marker tampering raise BoundaryFailure.
A compiling semantic mutation fails actual Java assertions; invalid Java fails compilation; both leave the source fixture unchanged.
An after-version preview contains no changes and approved apply returns no_change.
Demo JSON contains 8 hashed artifact payloads, an applied receipt and already_applied replay status; hashes reconcile with artifact bytes before temporary cleanup.
hints: Start with the input contract: owned fixture root, exact filenames, bounded bytes and a full sorted manifest. Calculate identity before planning any rewrite.
A patch is review text; the executable plan must additionally bind exact after-content, source identity and actual before/candidate Java receipts. Test a mutation that compiles but changes totals.

Separate credential resolution from actor fields, and sign all binding fields. Replay requires both a remembered approved result and a matching resulting snapshot; stale dependencies invalidate review.
answer: I would deliver a narrow evidence-producing accelerator rather than imply that one text substitution modernizes an enterprise application. The executable slice owns only disposable Java fixtures. It manifests every permitted input, records a coverage-qualified local dependency graph and plans one audited removal of an immediately unboxed local Integer. Dry run copies candidates and actually compiles/runs before and after;43 Java assertions and an observed signature establish the stated fixture contract. Approval resolves a credential through a trusted fixture mapping and signs actor, root, preview, input and patch identities. Apply rejects unknown plans, changed bytes, forged approvals and drift anywhere in the snapshot, validates again and replaces one owned file. In-process replay is observable and produces no second write. The artifact bundle includes patch, receipts, graph gaps and hashes. I would defend the limits: lexical references are not complete call resolution, tests are finite coverage, demo identity is not enterprise authentication and replay state is not crash-durable. Git/CI and other-language integrations need explicit adapters, isolated workspaces, actual validation and independent review before any real repository action.

followups.question: What must change before this can accept a real Java repository?
followups.answer: Add a separately authorized workspace boundary and a supported build-system/compiler adapter. Capture the base revision, dirty state, dependencies and complete applicable input set. Use compiler-aware symbol/rewrite analysis with explicit gaps, fixture-independent behavioral contracts, integration tests and dependency validation. Isolate untrusted build execution; a timeout and Java heap flag do not form an OS sandbox. Replace the readable demo credential with independently authenticated identity and protected approval signing. Define concurrency, multi-file atomicity, restart recovery and rollback. Recompute evidence on the exact reviewed bytes. The case should remain unable to write arbitrary repositories until these capabilities and permissions are concrete; expanding the path parameter alone would bypass the essential boundary.

followups.question: How could Python orchestrate.NETor AI-assisted modernization without asking me to implement.NETcode?
followups.answer: Define a target adapter that reports tool/runtime capabilities, supported constructs, input identity, coverage gaps, a deterministic proposed patch and actual build/test receipts. Python manages inventory, workspace isolation, review state and artifact schemas. Existing target-specific tools or an optional AI-assisted plugin may propose transformations, but a proposal is not evidence of behavior parity. Unsupported constructs and missing validators must block that slice or narrow its claim. Keep actor authorization and input/patch binding outside model-generated text. Document target-specific deployment/data rollback constraints. This is a design contract only in the current case: no .NET runtime is used, no C# implementation is required and no external AI model is called.

limits: Only Python 3.11+ standard library and an installed JDK supporting --release 17 are used. Java commands were executed locally with OpenJDK 23.0.2; no package, provider or network is needed after file download.
Only the exact audited pricing fixture is transformable. This is not a general Java source parser or semantic rewrite engine; identity-sensitive boxing examples outside that body are unsupported.
The graph is lexical local-class reference coverage only, not a complete method/call/build/dependency graph. External and reflective edges remain gaps.
All source writes target program-created temporary fixtures. This is not an OS security sandbox against malicious concurrent processes or edited executable code.
The demo credential is public fixture data. HMAC keys and replay records are process-local; this is no production identity, distributed approval, persistent replay or crash-recovery system.
Application is one-file atomic replacement only; no general multi-file transactional writer or rollback engine is implemented.
Runtime assertions prove the explicit 43-case fixture contract and finite sampled input behavior, not arbitrary application equivalence.
Git, CI delivery and other-language/.NET adapter contracts are design only. The program never commits, pushes, opens a pull request, touches an external repository or invokes an AI model.

execution.summary: Reference author ran eight self-tests from a newly extracted source bundle using Python 3.14.7 and OpenJDK 23.0.2 with --release 17. Successful gates compile the Java fixture and execute 43 behavior checks. Preview, approval binding, changed-input rejection, tampering rejection and process-local replay passed. This exercises only the supplied disposable fixture.
